ideas.description: Exploit: spend Muon's margin on resize, the cheapest accuracy-for-time lever. Resize costs ~0.4 pp/s (E008/E013/E018); cutting epochs costs ~0.75 pp/s (E020). Start from the I032 result if it was kept as the fused-Muon base, otherwise from E025 (commit 50d39d6: E024 tip plus Muon on the block conv filters, lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, 11 ep, batch 1536). Change only the 24 px fraction, from the first 50% of steps to the first 75% (bilinear antialias=True after flip and translate, LR/Lookahead/Muon schedules still tied to step count). Both shapes stay compiled and graphed in build, with no recompile in timed train. Report per-seed accuracy. This is the head-to-head alternative to I033 (epoch cut) for spending the same margin; if both run, compare pp lost per second saved.
ideas.expected: From a fused I032 base at ~6.7-6.8 s: time drops ~0.5-0.6 s, to ~6.1-6.25 s (24 px step ~0.68x of a 32 px step). Accuracy drops ~0.2-0.3 pp from ~0.762, to ~0.758-0.760. Feasible and a new best (tip 6.45 s). A loss <= 0.45 pp/s keeps H3.2.5 on the linear line. A loss > 0.6 pp/s means resize cost steepens at high fractions or interacts with Muon, and the epoch cut (I033) wins. From the unfused E025 base, expect ~6.7 s (not a new best, but the rate is still informative).

ideas.description: Explore the Muon x augmentation interaction (D007: C0074/C0075/C0077 report that Muon gains more than baseline optimizers from stronger augmentation, and that weak augmentation causes late spectral collapse). H4.1's 'weaker regularization is better at ~10 ep' was learned under SGD (E004, E011). Start from the I032 Muon base (or E025 if I032 is not kept). Change only the translate amplitude, from 2 px back to 4 px, in both resolution phases. Everything else stays fixed.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (+/-0.03 s). Accuracy -0.35 to +0.3 pp; the SGD prior (E011: translate 2 gave +0.35 pp) points down. A gain >= 0.3 pp means the optimizer flips the regularization optimum, so H4.1's conclusions must be re-measured on the Muon base (cutout 8 next). A loss >= 0.25 pp means the optimum carries over and H4.1 transfers to Muon.

ideas.description: Muon step size at a short horizon (D007: C0053/C0056/C0065). lr 0.24 / momentum 0.6 came from airbench94_muon's CIFAR-10 setting at batch 2000. Start from the I032 Muon base (or E025), 11 ep. Change only the Muon peak lr, from 0.24 to 0.32 (same schedule shape, same momentum). SGD on BN, biases and head stays unchanged.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged. Accuracy -0.3 to +0.35 pp. A gain >= 0.25 pp adds margin, which goes to the epoch or resize cut (I033 / 75%-at-24 px), and justifies a momentum 0.5 follow-up. A loss >= 0.25 pp puts the optimum at or below 0.24 and closes Muon lr tuning.

ideas.description: Noise floor on the current tip, which every near-threshold verdict depends on (E024 margin is only +0.14 pp; E023 showed same-seed spread of up to 0.9 pp per trial). Rerun E024 (commit 22da5d1) unchanged, twice. Pool the result with E024 and with E022/E023 (same math at batch 1024) to estimate the sd of a 3-seed mean and of a run-to-run difference. Report per-seed accuracy and time.
ideas.expected: No change in time (6.45 +/- 0.05 s). The 3-seed-mean accuracy falls within 0.7525-0.7565, and the 3-seed-mean sd is <= 0.25 pp. If a rerun falls below 0.753, the E024 tip is not reliably feasible: treat Muon-based margin as necessary, and require a >= 0.3 pp margin before any keep.

ideas.description: Explore depth vs. epochs, the one untested architecture axis. On the SGD tip E024 (128/256/704, 50% at 24 px, batch 1536, 11 ep), use 2 convs per block instead of 3 (drop the last conv of each block; the remaining structure, head and widths are unchanged). Raise the epochs so that the estimated per-run conv FLOPs match E024 (about 11 -> ~14.5 ep), and rescale the schedules to the new step count. Recapture the graphs in build.
ideas.expected: Time ~6.4-6.6 s (matched FLOPs, slightly more fixed per-step overhead). Accuracy most likely -0.2 to -0.6 pp: E017 showed epochs above 11 return only ~0.1 pp/ep, so depth is probably the better buy. Accuracy >= E024 within noise supports H1.2.3 and opens a shallower, faster family. A loss >= 0.4 pp refutes it and closes depth cuts.

drop.reason: E025 made block-3 widening on the SGD tip a dominated margin source. Muon gives +0.78 pp at 0.96 pp/s even unfused; block-3 896 is predicted at <= 0.75 pp/s, and 5/6 committee members forecast not-improved. Revisit only if the Muon line runs short of margin.

Pure margin builder at equal time on the SGD tip, with an expected effect (<= 0.3 pp) inside the unmeasured noise floor. Its value would only show in a later combination, and the base is likely moving to Muon, where the optimum may differ. 5/6 committee members forecast not-improved.

Same issue as I035: an equal-time accuracy tweak on the SGD tip, expected at +0-0.4 pp, close to noise, and it cannot improve the score on its own. H5.2 is low-priority now that Muon supplies margin more cheaply. Re-pose it on the Muon base if margin is ever needed.

Muon on the block convs has opened a new line: E025 gave +0.78 pp, and the time cost is launch overhead that I032 is fusing. The question now is how to spend that margin.

**Kept in the queue:**
- I033: Muon with the epoch cut to 9.5.
- I034: batch 2048.
- I038: one CUDA graph per resolution phase, which saves time at equal math and carries over to any base.

**New ideas:**
- **Muon + 75% of steps at 24 px (H3.2.5, P4).** This is the main competitor to I033. Resize costs about 0.4 pp per second saved, against about 0.75 pp/s for cutting epochs (E020). So on the measured rates, spending Muon's margin on a larger low-res fraction should beat spending it on epochs. Running both shows which way of spending the margin is cheaper.
- **Muon + translate 4 (H4.2, P2).** The literature says Muon benefits more from strong augmentation. This checks whether H4.1's weak-regularization optimum, learned under SGD, still holds under Muon.
- **Muon lr 0.32 (H4.2, P2).** The current value was carried over from the CIFAR-10 recipe at a different batch size and budget. This idea and the translate idea are both outside the committee's evidence; each is a clean single-axis test.
- **Noise-floor rerun of the E024 tip, twice (H1.1.3, P2).** The tip's margin over 0.753 is only +0.14 pp, and the same seed can vary by up to 0.9 pp per trial, so verdicts near the threshold need a measured noise floor.
- **2-conv blocks at matched FLOPs (H1.2.3, P1, explore).** This is the one architecture axis not yet tested.

**Dropped:** I035, I036 and I037. All three buy accuracy at equal time on the SGD tip, with expected gains near the noise floor. Muon now supplies margin more cheaply, and 5/6 committee members forecast none of the three improves the score.

**Ordering:** the Muon ideas depend on whether I032 is kept as the base, so the fused-Muon result should be checked first.
